title: Vaginal Itching

rationale.Physical Exam: Pelvic: Pale, thin vaginal mucosa, loss of rugae.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with vaginal itching, dryness, burning, dyspareunia, and increased urinary frequency. Postmenopausal. Exam reveals pale, thin vaginal mucosa with loss of rugae. Atrophic vaginitis results from estrogen deficiency → thinning of vaginal epithelium → decreased glycogen → loss of lactobacilli → increased vaginal pH → susceptibility to infection and irritation. Diagnosis is clinical. Wet mount may show increased WBCs and parabasal cells. Rule out other causes: candidiasis, bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis, STIs. Treatment: vaginal estrogen therapy (cream, ring, or tablet — first-line, minimal systemic absorption). Non-hormonal moisturizers and lubricants. If systemic vasomotor symptoms also present → consider systemic HRT.
